When and why did you start training for fighting? A taekwondo instructor moved near my house in 96. He took a few private lessons in jiu-jitsu. I never did taekwondo. He saw me and my friends hanging out around the neighborhood and asked my father to have them come wrestle with him. I never wanted to go and one day my dad was like if you don’t go he won’t stop asking me. So I did it to please my dad. When I went there he tapped me out and my mind started rolling and never stopped.

What ranks and titles have you held? Former UFC Lightweight Champion. Former UFC Welterweight Champion. Rumble on the Rock lightweight champion. I am the most decorated jiu-jitsu athlete in America. I am the first non-Brazilian to win the world championships at the black belt level. Received Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu black belt from Andre Pederneiras. The Ultimate Fighter season five and season 19 coach.

Do you have any heroes? I have had so many and still do. It wouldn’t be fair to say just one.  I have new influences everyday in life and fighting.

What is your favorite technique? My heart and mind are my most important things.  I know it doesn’t sound too original but I will prepare properly for each fight and never give up.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It feels great fighting in the UFC.  When I was younger that is the only place I wanted to fight professionally.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I went to school to learn some wrestling but wasn’t too serious about the academics.

attributes.title: Bobby Hoffman

qna.value:
Training Style

"Like I said, I started running more, swimming more and getting myself in shape. There won't be any repeat of the Smith fight. I get up at 6 AM. Do an hour and a half of cardio. Come back home and rest. At 10:00 get on the,mat and get some grappling in. Go home and get some sleep. Go to the boxing gym at 4. Head to Jiu-Jitsu practice at 6. Do some lifting from 7 to 8. Come home and then do it all over again."

UFC History

At UFC 27 Bobby lost a majority decision to former UFC World Heavyweight Champion Maurice Smith. "Maurice is a tough fighter, but I lost that fight myself because I ran out of gas... I came back home and started working out more than ever before. I've dropped to 250 and I won't have a conditioning problem ever again."

UFC 30 Hoffman gave The South African fighter Robinson a true introduction to UFC with a first round Right Elbow to the head that put Robinson down with 3:27 remaining in the first round. NJ Commission has since declared this match a no contest.

UFC 34: High Voltage - Bobby lost to Josh Barnett by submission due to strikes at 4:25 of round 2.

More Information

On fighting for the UFC: "It feels really great. I've been fighting all over the world. It feels really good. I've been over to Japan and it's pretty big over there but in the United States UFC is the big show. When I first started this is where I wanted to be. I wanted to be UFC champion so it feels awesome."

On how he got into MMA: "Actually I sat in jail for awhile on assault charges. I walked out of jail on a Wednesday after being locked up in solitary confinement for 92 straight days. I got out and walked into a gym where they were participating in shootfighting. I'd always been a great wrestler and athlete and they asked if I wanted to wrestle so I started wrestling with them. I went to a fight that Friday two days out of jail and someone said a heavyweight didn't show up. It was a professional fight. They asked if anyone in the crowd wanted to fight and I jumped in there and won and that's how my career started."

Bobby's main athletic background was in football and he even played half a season with the Cleveland Browns before getting cut. "I had a short lived career. I actually left college a year early for the damn NFL and didn't complete my education but that's a different story." Bobby attended Ellsworth Junior College and the University of Akron.

Bobby's MMA record is 17-3 and he is 6-1 in RINGS competition.

"My right hand is packed with dynamite and if I can unleash it, if I catch you with the son of a gun it's pretty much out. I'm pretty much convinced that if I can catch anyone between the temple and the back of the head I'm going to at least make them dizzy. My conditioning is such that not only can I KO a guy in 32 seconds but I've also knocked them out 8 to 9 minutes into the fight."

Favorite pastimes:
“I enjoy going to the beach with my pitbull and my girlfriend Patty.”

Do you have any heroes?
“I respect Tank Abbott for going to Pro Wrestling and making it big time. I respect Tito Ortiz because he walks the walk and talks the talk and has his shit going on.”

TRAINING: Wake up, either strength and conditioning in the morning or I drill techniques with a partner/coach. Come home, eat a big brunch, rest up and in the evening I go to the MMA gym to get my hard rounds. I put in about 4-5 hours a day in the gym as well as study a lot of film throughout the day.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I was wrestling in college and I was noticing many high-level wrestlers doing extraordinarily well in the sport. I started watching and becoming a fan. After my freshman year of wrestling in college, a buddy of mine asked if I was interested in taking a MMA fight. I said yes and that same day we went out to Lansing, Michigan and I fought. From that moment, I became hooked and have been competing since then. That was in 2010.

What ranks and titles have you held? None

Do you have any heroes? My brothers

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It has been a dream of mine to become a world champion. I want to fight the very best in the entire world and only in the UFC can I fight the absolute best. I gave up and sacrificed a tremendous amount for this opportunity, so to be able to compete in the UFC is huge for me. There is nothing else in the world I should be doing than fighting for the premier organization in the world. This opportunity means everything to me.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I went to college at Michigan State University, where I received a bachelor’s degree in Sociology

What was your job before you started fighting? I was a bouncer at a nightclub and a kickboxing/fitness instructor.

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? I was 14-0 as an amateur fighter and held three amateur titles.

Ranks in any martial arts styles: Two-stripe blue belt in Jiu-Jitsu, Division I Big Ten collegiate wrestler

Favorite grappling technique: Armbar

Favorite Striking technique: Superman punch

When and why did you start training for fighting? At the age of 13

Training: Wake up 8:30am, Breakfast, 10am - 12:15 Gym, Lunch, 14:45-17:00 Sleep, 17:45-21:20 Gym, Dinner, 23:30 Sleep

What professional titles have you held? Professional cooking assistant to my head chef fiancee (No MMA professional titles)

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? Placed 8 out of 32 at IMMAF Worlds in Las Vegas 2015 - Austrian state Champion 2015/16 - ⁠bronze medalist IMMAF Europeans 2018 - ⁠got finished just once in 24 Fights - ⁠record 18-6

Any belts / ranks in grappling disciplines? Brazilian Jiu Jitsu brown belt

Any belts / ranks in striking disciplines? ⁠IMMAF MMA black belt graduation, Kickboxing black belt

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? The fight against Tom Nolan. Toughest because I got knocked out the first time in my career and could mature a lot through that experience.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? Jon Jones. Expert in every aspect of the sport. Brutal elbows and oblique kicks.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? Yes. In Austria it’s called “commercial college.”

What was your job before you started fighting? I did a lot of different jobs: Waiter, detective, recruiter, real estate agent, self-employed (own bar), and worked my whole childhood and youth in all kinds of crafted work with my father.

Origin of nickname: “Fritz Treiber gave it to me. He said, ‘Such a friendly face turns into a killer inside the cage.”

Personal Life / Background: Driving a Sports quad, riding a downhill bike and doing some tricks (wheelie, etc), playing table tennis, spending time in the forest and in nature. It's best to grill next to a river and listen to nature. Family (also the family members who are not related by blood) is the most important thing in life for me. I’m always looking to help people in need, and also animals, because they are really helpless.

qna.value:
When and why did you start training for fighting? I didn’t start training because I had a problem with bullying or because I fell in love with martial arts. I started training MMA for fun and extra training for football. The discipline, the competition, and the challenge attracted me to stay on the warrior’s path.

What does it mean for you to fight for the UFC? It’s the biggest stage in mixed martial arts, and it’s an honor to compete here. But just being in the UFC wasn't my goal, I want to leave a mark. I'd like to think that this is the true beginning of my journey, not the end.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? I admire fighters who changed the sport through hard work, discipline, and consistency. I respect champions who stay humble and let their performances speak for themselves. I'm not really a fan of trash talk just for the sake of it, conflict needs to be real, not manufactured.

Do you have any heroes outside of fighting? I admire people who have achieved success through hard work, discipline, and dedication, regardless of their profession. Those qualities inspire me every day. You can admire hard work in any craft.

What are your current ranks in martial arts? I’ve trained in multiple martial arts for many years and continue to improve every day. I'm a brown belt in BJJ under my head coach Nemanja Milošević. For me, what matters most is what I do inside the cage.

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? I’ve won titles and earned victories against tough opponents throughout my career, but I believe my biggest accomplishments are still ahead of me. My goal is to make history in the UFC.

What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career and why? Every fight has helped shape my career, but the fight that opened the door to the UFC stands out the most. It proved that I belong among the best fighters in the world.

Is there a cause that you want to use your platform for? I want to inspire young people to get involved in sports and live healthy, disciplined lives. Martial arts can change lives, and I want to be a positive example

Beyond a championship or money, what motivates you? I became champion once and I will do so again. Money is just a consequence of greatness.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I dedicated my life to becoming a professional fighter, I am currently studying to get a boxing coach degree at the Serbian national college of physical education

What was your job before you started fighting? I was soccer player, before turning to MMA. In this period, MMA at Serbia was at a very low level and actually in one moment it was illegal. I constantly had a job during my career. Nowadays I’m a Beekeeper with more than 100 hives and an MMA champion at the same time.

Favorite grappling technique: Hands down, the guillotine choke.

Favorite striking technique: The Jab and the liver shot.

Tell us about your life outside of fighting: Outside of training, I enjoy spending time with my family and close friends. I also love nature and beekeeping, which helps me relax and stay grounded. Those moments help me recharge so I can give everything I have in training and competition.

qna.value:
TRAINING: Everything - Muay Thai, Boxing, Wrestling, BJJ, S&C, Cross Fit

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started MMA when I needed to get fit for the Royal Marines, so I searched the Internet for the toughest sports and MMA and Olympic wrestling came top of the list. That was my introduction to MMA at the Dragonslair Gym where I started training

What ranks and titles have you held? I currently hold the southwest Muay Thai boxing belt and am undefeated.

Do you have any heroes? Johnson Bahari, the only living soldier to have won the Victoria Cross Medal. I met him and he's a huge inspiration

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? Fighting in the UFC means everything to me. It’s my dream to do so; I only wish now for a successful career. I intend to invest in myself and find good coaches to teach me the skills to continue to improve

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I went to college to learn about sports science but I got behind and left for the Royal Marines

What was your job before you started fighting? I worked for Cooper Avon tires before my opportunity to fight in The Ultimate Fighter. I’m glad to have moved on.

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? Traveling out to Dubai earlier this year and being awarded KO of the Night and Fight of the Night on Cage Warriors, Knocking out Mok Rahman

Favorite grappling technique: Rear naked choke

Favorite striking technique: Straight right
